learn: "Hola" means hello. "Adiós" means goodbye. "Hasta luego" means see you later.
"Buenos días" is good morning, "buenas tardes" is good afternoon and "buenas noches" is good evening or good night.
In many Spanish-speaking countries, friends greet with a handshake, a hug or a kiss on the cheek.
lessons.try: Greet three classmates in Spanish using the right time of day.

learn: "¿Cómo te llamas?" means "What is your name?" Answer: "Me llamo..." (My name is...).
"Mucho gusto" means "Nice to meet you."
"¿De dónde eres?" means "Where are you from?" Answer: "Soy de..." (I am from...).
lessons.try: Introduce yourself to a partner with your name and where you are from.

learn: "¿Cómo estás?" means "How are you?" (to a friend). "¿Cómo está usted?" is the polite form.
Answers: "Bien" (well), "Muy bien" (very well), "Así así" (so-so), "Mal" (bad).
Polite words: "por favor" (please), "gracias" (thank you), "de nada" (you're welcome).
check: The polite way to ask an adult "how are you" is...
lessons.try: Act out a short conversation asking how someone is.

learn: The Spanish alphabet has 27 letters, including ñ (eñe), as in "niño" (boy).
Letters are named differently: a (ah), e (eh), i (ee), o (oh), u (oo).
Spelling your name in Spanish is a useful skill.
lessons.try: Spell your name aloud using Spanish letter names.

learn: Spanish vowels each have one clear sound: a as in "father", e as in "met", i as in "see", o as in "go", u as in "food".
The letter h is always silent: "hola" sounds like "ola".
"ll" sounds like the y in "yes": "llamo". "j" sounds like a strong h: "jugo".
lessons.try: Read a list of Spanish words aloud, focusing on vowels.

learn: Accent marks show which syllable to stress: "teléfono".
Accents can change meaning: "si" (if) and "sí" (yes).
Upside-down marks begin questions and exclamations: ¿...? and ¡...!
lessons.try: Write three questions with correct punctuation.

learn: Uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco, seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez.
Teens: once, doce, trece... Tens: veinte, treinta, cuarenta, cincuenta... cien (100).
Combine tens and ones: treinta y cinco (35).
lessons.try: Count by tens to 100 in Spanish.

learn: Days: lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado, domingo.
Months: enero, febrero, marzo, abril, mayo, junio, julio, agosto, septiembre, octubre, noviembre, diciembre.
In Spanish, days and months are not capitalised.
lessons.try: Write this week's days with a Spanish activity for each.

learn: "¿Cuál es la fecha?" means "What is the date?"
Dates go day then month: "Es el cinco de mayo" (It's the 5th of May).
"¿Cuándo es tu cumpleaños?" means "When is your birthday?"
check: In Spanish dates, the day comes...
At the end of the year
lessons.try: Ask three classmates their birthdays in Spanish.

learn: Rojo (red), azul (blue), amarillo (yellow), verde (green), negro (black), blanco (white), anaranjado (orange), morado (purple).
Colors come after the noun: "el lápiz rojo" (the red pencil).
Some colors change ending to match: "la casa roja" (the red house).
lessons.try: Name the colors of five things in your room.

learn: El libro (book), el cuaderno (notebook), el lápiz (pencil), la mochila (backpack), la mesa (table), la silla (chair).
"El" and "la" both mean "the": el for masculine, la for feminine nouns.
"¿Qué es esto?" means "What is this?"
lessons.try: Label ten objects in your room with Spanish sticky notes.

learn: To make plurals, add -s after a vowel (libros) or -es after a consonant (papeles).
"Los" and "las" are the plural forms of "el" and "la".
"Hay" means "there is" or "there are": "Hay tres libros."
lessons.try: Describe your backpack using "hay".

learn: Madre (mother), padre (father), hermano (brother), hermana (sister), abuelo (grandfather), abuela (grandmother).
Tío and tía are uncle and aunt; primo and prima are cousins.
"Tengo dos hermanos" means "I have two brothers (or siblings)."
lessons.try: Draw your family tree with Spanish labels.

learn: Alto (tall), bajo (short), simpático (nice), inteligente (intelligent), divertido (fun).
Adjectives match the person: "Él es alto." "Ella es alta."
Use "muy" for very: "muy simpática".
lessons.try: Describe a family member using three adjectives.

learn: Mi (my), tu (your), su (his/her/their).
"Mi madre" means my mother; "mis hermanos" means my brothers.
Add -s when the noun is plural.
lessons.try: Write five sentences about your family using mi and mis.

units.t: The Verb Ser and Subject Pronouns

learn: Yo (I), tú (you, friend), usted (you, polite), él (he), ella (she).
Nosotros (we), ellos (they, masculine or mixed), ellas (they, feminine).
Spanish often drops the pronoun because the verb shows who: "Soy" = I am.
lessons.try: Point to people around you and say the right pronoun.

learn: Ser means "to be" for lasting traits: yo soy, tú eres, él/ella/usted es.
Nosotros somos, ellos/ellas/ustedes son.
Use ser for identity, origin, description and time.
lessons.try: Write a sentence with each form of ser.

learn: Put "no" before the verb: "No soy alto."
Questions can use the same words with rising voice: "¿Eres de México?"
Answer: "Sí, soy de México" or "No, no soy de México."
lessons.try: Ask and answer three yes-or-no questions.

learn: Matemáticas, ciencias, historia, inglés, arte, música, educación física.
"Mi clase favorita es arte" means "My favourite class is art."
"Me gusta" means "I like": "Me gusta la música."
lessons.try: Make a list of your classes in Spanish and star your favourite.

learn: "¿Qué hora es?" means "What time is it?"
"Es la una" (It's 1:00). "Son las tres" (It's 3:00). "Son las cuatro y media" (4:30).
"¿A qué hora es la clase?" asks what time the class is.
lessons.try: Draw five clocks and write the time in Spanish.

learn: Por la mañana (in the morning), por la tarde (in the afternoon).
"Tengo matemáticas a las nueve" means "I have maths at nine."
Describe your schedule with times and subjects.
lessons.try: Write your school-day schedule in Spanish.

learn: El pan (bread), el queso (cheese), la manzana (apple), el arroz (rice), el pollo (chicken), el agua (water), la leche (milk), el jugo (juice).
Meals: el desayuno (breakfast), el almuerzo (lunch), la cena (dinner).
"Tengo hambre" means "I'm hungry"; "Tengo sed" means "I'm thirsty."
lessons.try: Write your favourite breakfast in Spanish.

learn: "Quisiera..." means "I would like..." "Para mí, una ensalada" means "For me, a salad."
"¿Cuánto cuesta?" means "How much does it cost?"
"La cuenta, por favor" means "The bill, please."
lessons.try: Role-play ordering lunch at a café with a partner.

learn: "Me gusta el chocolate" (I like chocolate). "Me gustan las uvas" (I like grapes: plural).
"No me gusta" means "I don't like".
"¿Te gusta...?" asks "Do you like...?"
check: "Me gustan las uvas" uses gustan because uvas is...
lessons.try: Survey classmates about foods they like and dislike.

learn: An infinitive is the basic form of a verb, like "hablar" (to speak).
Spanish infinitives end in -ar, -er or -ir.
Common -ar verbs: hablar, estudiar, bailar, cantar, caminar, escuchar.
lessons.try: List ten -ar verbs with their English meanings.

learn: Drop -ar and add endings: yo -o, tú -as, él/ella -a, nosotros -amos, ellos -an.
Hablar: hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, hablan.
"Yo estudio español" means "I study Spanish."
lessons.try: Conjugate "cantar" in all forms.

learn: "¿Escuchas música?" (Do you listen to music?) "Sí, escucho música."
Add time words: siempre (always), a veces (sometimes), nunca (never).
Write sentences about your weekly routine.
lessons.try: Write five sentences about what you do after school.

learn: Spanish is an official language in 20 countries, including Spain, Mexico, Argentina, Colombia and Peru.
Over 500 million people speak Spanish, and many millions live in the United States.
Spanish came from Latin, the language of ancient Rome.
lessons.try: Colour Spanish-speaking countries on a world map.

learn: Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) in Mexico honours loved ones who have died with altars, flowers and food.
La Tomatina in Spain is a tomato-throwing festival.
Many countries celebrate their independence days with parades and music.
check: Independence days are often celebrated with...
lessons.try: Research a festival from a Spanish-speaking country and present it.

learn: Spanish-speaking cultures gave the world flamenco, salsa, tango and mariachi music.
Foods include tacos, paella, empanadas and arepas.
Learning a language opens doors to new friends and cultures.
check: Learning a language opens doors to...
lessons.try: Listen to a piece of mariachi or flamenco music.
